Klohn Crippen Berger Ltd. (2017). Study of Tailings Management Technologies. MEND Report 2.50.1. Mine Environment Neutral Drainage (MEND) Program, prepared for The Mining Association of Canada and MEND; KCB project M10034A01.730, October 2017.

Locators are PRINTED page numbers (PDF page = printed + 32). A state-of-practice and risk study (164 pp) of conventional, thickened, high-density thickened, paste and filtered surface tailings facilities in Canada. The only quantitative cost table is Table 5.2 (p.44): indicative OPERATING cost per tonne of tailings stored by dewatering technology (typical total, range, and the processing-and-transport and dam-and-water components), capital and closure excluded; loaded as opex-total with min/max, components in other-values. The report states capital costs cannot be given and prints NO energy figures (no kWh/t for thickening, filtration or pumping), so nothing was loaded for energy or capex; separator_thickening-filtration, separator_tailings-reclaim and press_dewatering get NO energy or capex here. Traps: (1) "$" currency and price year are not stated (Canadian study; CAD and 2017 assumed, flagged in the unit and note). (2) Table 5.2 thickened total 1.20 does not equal its components (0.30 + 1.00 = 1.30). (3) The cost is for the whole disposal system (dewatering, transport, placement, dam and water management), not the dewatering equipment alone, so it is not an equipment opex. (4) The paste typical total (2.00) equals the bottom of its printed range (2.00-8.00). (5) Solids-content definitions differ between the executive summary, glossary and Table 4.1. Appendix II case histories and Table 4.1 hold no cost or energy numbers. No TRL.
